text.p: These are leading stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government insists that export of petroleum products to Sierra Leone is banned.
- Nigeria's 138 insurance companies need 11 billion naira before January if they are to meet a deadline to increase their capital bases.

- Importation of palm oil, mostly from Malaysia, is costing Nigeria huge sums of money every year as well as depriving local people of jobs, the Agricultural and Allied Senior Staff Association claims.
- Nigerian Stock Exchange revives plan for Abuja trading floor.
- Workers at the Department of Petroleum Resources say fuel shortages would be eliminated if proper funding were provided for the sector.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani admits that Nigeria's economy has not bounced back from recession despite a certain measure of financial stability.
- A shipment of locomotives for the Nigerian Railways Corporation is expected to arrive at the Apapa port in Lagos this week.
- Private airlines want a review of Nigeria's bilateral air service agreements to allow them to fly to more international destinations.
- An institutional investor in Afprint has concluded arrangements to sell a 6.25 percent stake in the textile company. The identity of the investor is unclear.
